subject: MAP: final implementation plan and sign-off for ParcelPay
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@parcelpay.com>, Michael O'Leary <mike.oleary@parcelpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Quick recap + draft MAP (next steps)

Hi Julia / Mike —

Thanks again for taking time today. Attached is the draft Mutual Action Plan (ParcelPay_MAP_v3.xlsx) that captures the milestones we discussed, owners, and the target timeline. I pulled the key items into this email so we have a single view: 

- Target close: 2026-02-26 (customer signature and PO)
- Go-live (prod traffic): 2026-03-30 (depends on infra readiness & security review)
- Success criteria: <1s 95th percentile latency on 8k token workflows; production embedding throughput >= 250 reqs/min; no PII leakage in eval test-set

Milestones (high level):
1) Procurement & contract signature — Julia (ParcelPay) / Marissa (Redwood) — target 2026-02-26
2) Security questionnaire & evidence — Julia + ParcelPay SecOps — complete by 2026-02-19
3) Private deployment prep (VPC peering, network diagram) — Dev (Redwood) — complete by 2026-02-24
4) Integration testing & perf validation — Rishi (Redwood) & ParcelPay eng — 2026-02-25 — 2026-03-20
5) Go-live readiness review and cutover window — All — 2026-03-25

Dependencies / open items we flagged on the call:
- ParcelPay to confirm VPC CIDR and firewall rules (network_diagram.pdf requested)
- ParcelPay legal to confirm PO process and billing contact
- ParcelPay to provide sample prompt sets and evaluation metrics for the QA run

Please review the MAP and let me know any edits. If you’re comfortable, confirm the target close and I’ll update the timeline + push for final signatures.

Attachments: ParcelPay_MAP_v3.xlsx, network_diagram.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0119

--
From: Julia Chen <julia.chen@parcelpay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael O'Leary <mike.oleary@parcelpay.com>, dev_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick recap + draft MAP (next steps)

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary. Two quick items from ParcelPay side: 

1) Procurement timeline looks tight for us — legal has a standing procurement sprint that ends 2026-02-28. We can aim to sign by 2026-03-01 rather than 02-26 unless we prioritize it. I can escalate if needed.
2) We confirmed the network CIDR; attaching the initial network diagram (see network_diagram.pdf). Our infra lead (Mike) will follow up with exact firewall rules.

On the success criteria, the latency target looks aggressive but reasonable — we'll start with the eval set you mentioned and push for 95th percentile under 1s.

Can you have Dev call out any additional infra prerequisites in the MAP? Also, is there a simple one-page SLA addendum we can sign that covers response times and support during cutover?

Thanks,
Julia
VP Product, ParcelPay
julia.chen@parcelpay.com

--
On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 15:12, marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> [original message]
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@parcelpay.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + draft MAP (next steps)

Hi Julia / Marissa —

Thanks for the diagram, Julia. A couple of technical clarifications to put into the MAP: 

- VPC peering vs. VPN: For the private deployment option you selected, we recommend VPC peering to avoid latency and to support high-throughput KV cache. If ParcelPay policy requires VPN due to compliance, there will be an additional 3–5 business day ops window to validate routing.
- Firewall: We need two outbound rules (443 to Redwood control plane IPs and 8443 to inference nodes). Please have the infra team open these to the IP ranges in the network_diagram.pdf.
- HSM/KMS integration: If you want Redwood to access keys via customer-managed KMS, we need a service account + IAM permission list. That typically takes 2 business days to confirm.

I'll update the MAP to show these as dependencies and add the ETA delta if ParcelPay chooses VPN.

Attachments referenced: network_diagram.pdf

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Julia Chen <julia.chen@parcelpay.com>, Michael O'Leary <mike.oleary@parcelpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:33:00 -0500
Subject: Updated MAP (v3 -> v4) + SLA addendum draft

Hi Julia / Mike —

Thanks for the fast responses. I attached an updated MAP (ParcelPay_MAP_v3.xlsx -> v4 inside the file) and a one-page SLA addendum (SLA_addendum.docx) that covers support hours, an escalation contact during cutover, and response SLAs for Sev1 issues during the first 30 days. Highlights of changes: 

- Procurement target moved to 2026-03-01 to match ParcelPay legal cadence (Julia confirmed)
- Added "VPN vs VPC" dependency and two possible timeline tracks: 
  a) VPC peering: keep original timeline (close 03-01, go-live 03-30)
  b) VPN: +7 business days on infra validation; go-live moves to 04-10
- Added HSM permission checklist for KMS integration (Dev)
- Rishi added integration test windows and a perf validation checklist (see MAP milestone 4)

Ask: Please confirm which network option you prefer (VPC peering or VPN) and whether ParcelPay can sign the SLA addendum at the same time as the PSA. If yes, I’ll route DocuSign for signature and lock the close date.

If there are no further edits, can I treat this as final and request exec sign-off next week?

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: ParcelPay_MAP_v3.xlsx (updated to v4), SLA_addendum.docx

From: Michael O'Leary <mike.oleary@parcelpay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Julia Chen <julia.chen@parcelpay.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Updated MAP (v3 -> v4) + SLA addendum draft

Marissa / team —

Thanks — ParcelPay prefers VPC peering. We reviewed the SLA addendum internally and are fine signing that alongside the PSA. Confirming these points: 

- Procurement: ParcelPay legal will prioritize the PSA and SLA for 2026-03-01 signature. I will be the internal approver and will confirm PO contact once legal is done.
- Network: VPC peering approved; infra will provide the final firewall rules and peering request by 2026-02-18.
- Go-live: we’re aligned on the go-live target of 2026-03-30 (assuming no major perf regressions in testing).

We consider the MAP agreed for commercial & technical milestones. Please send the DocuSign link for the PSA + SLA when you’re ready and we’ll sign.

Regards,
Mike O'Leary
VP Engineering — ParcelPay
mike.oleary@parcelpay.com
